Like LiF, its fluoride anions resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2, and Si(IV) is hard to reduce, so it should resist the sulfide electrolyte. It has no P, B or S-O channel, which are the product channels behind the earlier penalties. The main risk is SiF4 or Si-S products.
proposals.motivation: The best penalties so far were LiF (0.189) and Li3BO3 (0.204), both still well above the 0.05 threshold. The failures came from S/Cl/P-releasing contact products. Li6Zr2O7 (0.31) and Li2O (1.82) showed that a simple oxide is not enough. A fluorosilicate combines the fluoride anion chemistry that worked best with a tetravalent, non-reducible cation, which is a modest step from LiF.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2SiF6 is a wide-gap fluorosilicate with fully oxidized Si(IV) and F(-) anions. Like LiF, its fluoride anions resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2, and Si(IV) is hard to reduce, so it should resist the sulfide electrolyte. It has no P, B or S-O channel, which are the product channels behind the earlier penalties. The main risk is SiF4 or Si-S products.
proposal.motivation: The best penalties so far were LiF (0.189) and Li3BO3 (0.204), both still well above the 0.05 threshold. The failures came from S/Cl/P-releasing contact products. Li6Zr2O7 (0.31) and Li2O (1.82) showed that a simple oxide is not enough. A fluorosilicate combines the fluoride anion chemistry that worked best with a tetravalent, non-reducible cation, which is a modest step from LiF.

proposal.hypothesis: LiMgCl3 is a wide-gap chloride with the same anion as the Li6PS5Cl electrolyte and a non-reducible Mg2+ cation. Compared with Li2MgCl4, it has a higher Li:Mg ratio and no extra Cl-rich channel, so it may keep the sulfide-contact penalty low. Chloride oxidation at 4.0 V should also be better than sulfide oxidation.
proposal.motivation: Li2MgCl4 (mp-aaaacffw) was the lowest-penalty chloride, at 0.081 (bin 4), and it was closer to the 0.05 target than the fluoride (0.189) or borate (0.204) coatings. Its remaining products (LiF, SCl, PF5) suggest that Mg-chloride chemistry is promising but needs a composition adjustment.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZnCl4 is a chloride analogue of the best coating so far, Li2MgCl4 (penalty 0.081, bin 4). It keeps the same Cl anion as the Li6PS5Cl electrolyte, avoiding the S/P/F-releasing channels that drove the other penalties, and it is a wide-gap insulator. Zn2+ may change the contact energetics, so it is a targeted test of whether the chloride family can reach the 0.05 threshold.
proposal.motivation: Li2MgCl4 (mp-aaaacffw) had the lowest penalty of any evaluated coating (0.081, bin 4), well below the fluoride (0.337), borate (0.204) and silicate (0.725) results. LiMgCl3 (0.189) was worse, so the Li:Mg ratio is not the only factor and a cation swap is worth testing.
